Text | Fanyu Meng, Er Mu

Editing | Er Mu, Fanyu Meng

This is the best interactive science explainer I have ever come across. Every concept comes with an animation you can play with, which makes it wonderfully intuitive and vivid. It is the work of Bartosz Ciechanowski, a mysterious genius I know nothing else about. Here is the link:

https://ciechanow.ski/sound/

Hopefully it loads in mainland China.

The author starts with the motion of particles and builds up the phenomena and basic concepts of acoustics from the ground up. Note that you can drag the little balls in the animations below.

We have covered many of these basic concepts in earlier posts on our WeChat account, so I have added links in parentheses after the corresponding concepts below.

The site explains, very systematically, the frequency, amplitude and phase of sound waves, interference, reflection and other phenomena; sound pressure (What on earth is a decibel (dB), and why 1 + 1 ≠ 2), sound intensity (What is sound intensity?) and how sound pressure and intensity levels are calculated; and string vibration, modes, harmonics, the Doppler effect (Doppler, the man who raced against sound) and timbre (What is timbre?). It even touches on signal processing, with the Fourier transform, the Gibbs phenomenon and more.

On how sound is produced, we also have two articles:

How musical instruments make sound: woodwinds, the flute

How do we produce our voices?

It even has a real-time spectrum analyzer! That is just ridiculous.

Our institute once developed a similar interactive teaching app, and so did TUM. For some reason, though, neither of them will open anymore.

https://gershwin.akustik.rwth-aachen.deitapp/
